title: Working Out What One Payroll Period Recovers on an Employee Meal Account
content:
The amount one payroll period recovers on an Employee Meal Account is worked out from that account's own ledger of charges accrued and recoveries remitted, and from nothing else.

## 1. The balance standing

The balance standing is every charge accrued on the account to date less every recovery already remitted on it, and it is never read as less than nothing.

## 2. The recoverable balance

The recoverable balance is that same balance standing, so an ordinary period offers for recovery everything the account still owes.

## 3. The recovery ceiling

The recovery ceiling is the deduction ceiling printed against the meal plan the account is held on.

## 4. The employer's dining programme

Nothing of the recoverable balance is treated as met by the employer's dining programme at the account's site.

## 5. Deferral

Nothing of the period's recovery is deferred into a later period.

## 6. Assembling the figure

The amount recovered is worked out in this order and in no other: the part the employer's programme meets is taken off the recoverable balance first, and that remainder, never read as less than nothing, is then held to the recovery ceiling; the deferred part is taken off the held figure next, and that result, again never read as less than nothing, is finally held to the balance standing. The figure is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end, and no intermediate step is rounded.

## 7. The period the remittance belongs to, and an empty account

The payroll period a remittance is made for is the period carried by the most recent charge accrued on the account. An account carrying no charge awaiting recovery has nothing to recover and no entry is made.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take an account whose ledger shows charges accrued to date of $318.40 and recoveries remitted to date of $96.00, held on a plan whose printed deduction ceiling is taken for this illustration as $140.00. The balance standing is $318.40 less $96.00, or $222.40, and the recoverable balance is the same $222.40. Nothing is met by the employer's programme, so the first step leaves $222.40; held to the recovery ceiling of $140.00 that becomes $140.00; nothing is deferred, so $140.00 stands; and held finally to the balance standing of $222.40 it remains $140.00. Rounded once at the end, the period recovers $140.00.

Take instead an account whose charges accrued to date are $52.00 and whose recoveries remitted to date are $52.00. The balance standing is nothing, the recoverable balance is nothing, and the figure recovered is nothing, so no entry is made.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
